questions.subject: English
questions.stem:
When I was a young girl, I lost my mother. There was nobody to look after and guide me. My father was a busy man and got married again. In those days people never considered education essential for girls, so I never went to school. I got married very young and had children. I became very busy. Later I had grandchildren and always felt so much happiness in cooking and feeding all of you. At times I used to regret not going to school, so I made sure that my children and grandchildren studied well...

Choose the option that best completes this sentence: By holding that people in those days did not treat education as necessary for girls, the grandmother is really showing that... (A) her father did not want her to study (B) she had not wanted to learn when she was a girl (C) her inability to read was the result of the customs of her time and not of any fault in her (D) she believed that girls should learn only household work

answerScheme.modelAnswer: her inability to read was the result of the customs of her time and not of any fault in her

evidence: In those days people never considered education essential for girls, so I never went to school.
At times I used to regret not going to school, so I made sure that my children and grandchildren studied well
I felt very dependent and helpless.

options.A: her father did not want her to study
options.B: she had not wanted to learn when she was a girl
options.C: her inability to read was the result of the customs of her time and not of any fault in her
options.D: she believed that girls should learn only household work

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: An old woman in your colony has never been to school and has just learnt to read at the age of sixty-two. Write an article of about 100 words for your school magazine on why age is no bar to learning, using her example.

markingPoints.description: Content: the article gives a clear view that age is no bar to learning and supports it with the example of a woman who learnt to read at sixty-two
Format: the correct format of a magazine article, that is, a striking heading and short paragraphs
Organisation: a clear beginning that states the main point, a middle part that gives the example and a short concluding thought
Accuracy: correct spelling, punctuation and capital letters, and a formal and simple tone
Expression: simple sentences and suitable vocabulary that hold the reader's attention

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
Learning Is Never Too Late

When my grandmother was sixty-two years old, she decided to learn the Kannada alphabet. She had never been to school, and for years she had felt helpless because she could not read. Her own granddaughter became her teacher, and every day she read, repeated, wrote and recited. On Saraswati Puja day during Dassara she opened a gift and read the title Kashi Yatre by Triveni by herself. She then touched her granddaughter's feet and said she was touching the feet of a teacher. Age is only a number. What matters is the determination to begin.

evidence: at this age of sixty-two you want to learn the alphabet?
For learning there is no age bar.
She would read, repeat, write, and recite.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Your village is opening a free evening class in which students will teach reading to people who have never been to school. Write an advertisement of about 100 words for a local newspaper, inviting those people to join and asking students to volunteer as teachers.

markingPoints.description: Content: the advertisement invites people who have never been to school to join the class and asks students to volunteer as teachers
Format: the correct format of an advertisement, that is, a bold catchy heading and short, clear sentences that call for action
Organisation: the details are arranged logically, that is, what the class offers, who may join, when it meets and how students can help
Accuracy: correct spelling, punctuation and capital letters, and a formal tone suitable for a newspaper advertisement
Expression: simple sentences and lively vocabulary that persuade readers to join the class or to volunteer

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
LEARN TO READ THIS EVENING

Do you wish to read a novel on your own? Then come to the village hall, where a free evening class begins this week. Any adult who has never been to school is welcome, because for learning there is no age bar. The class will meet after the day's work is over. Students of the school who can read and write are invited to volunteer as teachers. A little patience from a young person can give an old person the greatest happiness. Come and give the gift of reading to someone in your own family.

evidence: My grandmother, Krishtakka, never went to school so she could not read.
For learning there is no age bar.
I was her only teacher and she was my first student.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem:
I looked at her face. It was unhappy and her eyes were filled with tears. She was a good-looking lady who was usually always smiling. Even today, I cannot forget the worried expression on her face. I leaned forward and held her hand.

Choose the option that best explains why the speaker says she cannot forget the worried expression on her grandmother’s face even today. (A) Because her grandmother had been unhappy for many years. (B) Because she had never seen her grandmother look unhappy before. (C) Because that expression was the same one her grandmother wore every day. (D) Because she was angry with her grandmother for crying.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Because she had never seen her grandmother look unhappy before.

evidence: I looked at her face. It was unhappy and her eyes were filled with tears.
She was a good-looking lady who was usually always smiling.
Even today, I cannot forget the worried expression on her face.

options.A: Because her grandmother had been unhappy for many years.
options.B: Because she had never seen her grandmother look unhappy before.
options.C: Because that expression was the same one her grandmother wore every day.
options.D: Because she was angry with her grandmother for crying.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Why was the grandmother so eager to know what happened next in the story of Kashi Yatre?

markingPoints.description: She identified herself with the novel’s protagonist, because the old lady in the story too wanted to go to Kashi
The grandmother herself had never gone to Kashi
So she was the one most interested in knowing what happened next and insisted that the serial was read out to her

answerScheme.modelAnswer: She identified herself with the novel’s protagonist, because the old lady in the story, like her, wanted ardently to go to Kashi. The grandmother too had never gone to Kashi. So she was more interested than anybody in knowing what happened next and used to insist that the serial was read out to her.

evidence: It is the story of an old lady and her ardent desire to go to Kashi or Varanasi.
My grandmother too never went to Kashi, and she identified herself with the novel’s protagonist.
So more than anybody else she was the one most interested in knowing what happened next in the story and used to insist that I read the serial out to her.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: The narrator calls her grandmother her first student. Why does she say so, and what does she add about her own future?

markingPoints.description: She was the one who taught the grandmother the Kannada alphabet, so the grandmother was her first student
She adds that she little knew then that she would one day become a teacher in Computer Science
She says she would teach hundreds of students

answerScheme.modelAnswer: She says so because she was the one who taught the grandmother the Kannada alphabet, so the grandmother was her first pupil. She adds that she little knew then that she would one day become a teacher in Computer Science and teach hundreds of students.

evidence: The next day onwards I started my tuition.
I was her only teacher and she was my first student.
Little did I know then that one day I would become a teacher in Computer Science and teach hundreds of students.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Why did the narrator feel that her grandmother’s gesture of touching her feet was not correct?

markingPoints.description: The tradition is that elders never touch the feet of youngsters
People touch the feet of God, elders and teachers as a mark of respect
Here the grandmother, an elder, touched the feet of her granddaughter, so the roles were reversed and the narrator felt it was not correct

answerScheme.modelAnswer: The tradition is that elders never touch the feet of youngsters; people touch the feet of God, elders and teachers as a mark of respect. Here a grandmother, an elder, touched the feet of her granddaughter, a youngster. The narrator felt that the roles had been reversed and that this was not correct.

evidence: never touch the feet of youngsters.
touched the feet of God, elders, and teachers.
tradition but today the reverse had happened. It was not correct.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: In the village where the speaker stayed as a girl of about twelve, the morning paper reached the house only in the afternoon and the weekly magazine came one day late. Why was this so?

markingPoints.description: The transport system in those days was not very good
The bus came with the papers, the weekly magazines and the post, and it reached the village late
So the morning paper was available only in the afternoon and the weekly magazine came one day late

answerScheme.modelAnswer: The transport system in those days was not very good. The bus that came with the papers, the weekly magazines and the post reached the village late, so the morning paper could be had only in the afternoon, and the weekly magazine came one day late.

evidence: Those days, the transport system was not very good, so we used to get the morning paper only in the afternoon.
The weekly magazine used to come one day late.
All of us would wait eagerly for the bus, which used to come with the papers, weekly magazines and the post.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: The narrator reminds her grandmother that at sixty-two her hair is grey, her hands are wrinkled, she wears spectacles and she works so much in the kitchen. Trace in steps how the grandmother’s reply answers these doubts, and show what the exchange reveals about learning.

markingPoints.description: The narrator’s first three doubts were that the grandmother’s hair was grey, her hands were wrinkled and she wore spectacles
Her fourth doubt was that the grandmother worked so much in the kitchen
The grandmother did not argue with any of these points; she only smiled
She gave her reason: for a good cause, if you are determined, you can overcome any obstacle
She promised to work harder than anybody and then stated that for learning there is no age bar
The exchange therefore shows that determination, not age, decides what a person can achieve

answerScheme.modelAnswer: 1. The narrator doubted the plan because at sixty-two the grandmother was already old: her hair was grey, her hands were wrinkled and she wore spectacles. 2. She added a fourth difficulty, that the grandmother worked so much in the kitchen. 3. The grandmother did not argue with any of these points. 4. She only smiled and gave one reason: for a good cause, if you are determined, you can overcome any obstacle. 5. She promised to work harder than anybody but said she would do it. 6. She then stated the lesson plainly: for learning there is no age bar. So the exchange shows that determination, not years or grey hair, decides what a person can achieve.

evidence: ‘Avva, at this age of sixty-two you want to learn the alphabet? All your hair is grey, your hands are wrinkled, you wear spectacles and you work so much in the kitchen...’
Childishly I made fun of the old lady. But she just smiled.
‘For a good cause if you are determined, you can overcome any obstacle. I will work harder than anybody but I will do it. For learning there is no age bar.’

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Trace in steps how the narrator’s attitude towards her grandmother’s learning changed from the day she laughed at the plan to the Dassara festival, giving the reason for each change.

markingPoints.description: At the start the narrator laughed at the plan, pointing to the grandmother’s grey hair and wrinkled hands at sixty-two, and made fun of the old lady
The narrator then went to a wedding and stayed a week, so she was away when the grandmother needed help
On her return she found her grandmother in tears and learnt that the grandmother had felt helpless and had said, If only I was educated enough
Her attitude changed to sympathy and she began tuition the next day, becoming the grandmother’s only teacher
On Dassara the grandmother touched her feet, saying that she was touching the feet of a teacher and not of her granddaughter
The narrator returned the namaskara and knew that her first student had passed with flying colours

answerScheme.modelAnswer: 1. When the grandmother announced that she would learn the Kannada alphabet, the narrator laughed at her, said that at sixty-two her hair was grey and her hands were wrinkled, and made fun of the old lady. 2. Then the narrator went to a wedding and stayed a week. 3. On her return she found her grandmother in tears and learnt that, while she was away, the grandmother had felt helpless and had said, If only I was educated enough. 4. Her attitude changed to sympathy, and she began tuition the next day and became her only teacher. 5. On Dassara the grandmother touched her feet, calling her a teacher and not a granddaughter. 6. The narrator returned the namaskara and knew that her first student had passed with flying colours.

evidence: Childishly I made fun of the old lady. But she just smiled.
But I knew it was not possible. If only I was educated enough.
She opened it and read immediately the title Kashi Yatre by Triveni and the publisher’s name. I knew then that my student had passed with flying colours.
